title: A certified lower bound on the quantum-capacity threshold of the depolarizing channel
abstract: The noise threshold below which the qubit depolarizing channel retains positive quantum capacity has been studied since 1996, and every improvement to date -- most recently the record of Agarwal et al. -- rests on floating-point evaluation of the coherent information. We give the first proven positivity results in this regime: an explicit 45-copy rank-two input state A, published as a 1,472-byte witness, with certified $I_c>0$ at the exact rational $p=16239/250000=0.064956$ (per-Pauli convention; total error rate $3p=0.194868$), beyond the best previously reported numerical value. Because the depolarizing family is a semigroup under composition, fixed-input coherent information is nonincreasing in $p$ on $[0,1/4]$, so a single certified point extends to the entire interval below it. The same machinery confines the positivity boundaries of A and of the strongest public state of Agarwal et al. to disjoint rational intervals separated by more than $1/25000$ -- to our knowledge the first proven ordering of two competing code states. Every computational claim in the paper reduces to a finite list of big-integer comparisons, checkable by a dependency-free few-hundred-line verifier whose soundness rests on three self-contained half-page lemmas. Payloads, certificates, and verifier accompany the paper as a supplementary artifact.
summary: This paper establishes the most rigorously proven lower bound on the noise threshold for the qubit depolarizing channel's positive quantum capacity. It achieves this by developing a novel mathematical framework that replaces floating-point approximations with verifiable proofs using exact rational arithmetic. This work is significant for setting new, provable benchmarks in quantum communication theory.
main_problem: The primary goal is to determine a certified lower bound on the noise threshold below which the quantum capacity of the qubit depolarizing channel remains positive.
main_result: The authors provide a rigorously proven, certified lower bound for the positive quantum capacity at $p=0.064956$, surpassing previous numerical estimates and establishing a provable ordering between competing code states.
method: The proof relies on constructing explicit mathematical 'certificates' using exact rational arithmetic (big-integer comparisons) to certify that the coherent information remains positive, avoiding floating-point approximations entirely.
model_or_system: The system analyzed is the qubit depolarizing channel, $D_p(ho)$, which models noise in quantum communication. The analysis uses concepts from quantum information theory involving tensor products and entropy calculations.
key_observables: Quantum capacity ($Q$), Coherent Information ($I_c$), and the noise parameter $p$ (per-Pauli convention).
important_parameters: The critical threshold value is certified at $p=16239/250000 = 0.064956$. The analysis is restricted to the interval $[0, 1/4]$ due to monotonicity.
main_assumptions: The claims are based on exact rational arithmetic proofs; no claim of optimality over all possible states or an exact threshold value is made.
figures_summary: Not specified in detail, but the notes mention Table 1 comparing literature bounds and Table 2 showing certified enclosures for $I_c$ at specific rational points.
paper_structure: The paper develops a rigorous framework involving multiple lemmas (A1-A3, E1-E4) to bound entropy using spectral confinement derived from exact matrix algebra. The structure culminates in the certification of the positive coherent information value via a dependency-free verifier.
why_interesting: This work represents a significant methodological advance by applying rigorous, computationally verifiable proof techniques (exact rational arithmetic) to quantum capacity problems, setting a new standard for theoretical bounds in open quantum systems.
